## Brock Purdy carves up the Vikings’ D with 3 TD passes in the 49ers’ 35-10 win in Mexico City
MEXICO CITY (AP) — Brock Purdy carved up the NFL’s stingiest defense with three touchdown passes in the first half and the [San Francisco 49ers](https://apnews.com/hub/san-francisco-49ers) beat the [Minnesota Vikings](https://apnews.com/hub/minnesota-vikings) 35-10 Sunday night in a matchup of NFC powerhouses.
The game played before a raucous crowd at historic Estadio Azteca [was billed as a matchup](https://apnews.com/article/vikings-49ers-preview-1f106876b69d919348cd0a7af2aa6d97) between one of the league’s most dangerous offenses in the 49ers (9-1) against a defense for the Vikings (7-3) that had rattled quarterbacks all season with an aggressive blitz package.
Coordinator Brian Flores’ schemes didn’t work at all against Purdy, who carved up the Minnesota defense for three touchdown drives on the Niners’ first four possessions. That helped the San Francisco build a 28-10 halftime lead thanks to a pick-6 by Ji’Ayir Brown against Kirk Cousins.
The Niners added the exclamation point in the second half with a 98-yard touchdown drive that featured “MVP!” chants for Purdy and was capped by Christian McCaffrey’s 6-yard run that made it 35-10 early in the fourth quarter.
Purdy finished 21 for 26 for 255 yards and a 146 passer rating that was more than double the league-low 69.5 rating that Minnesota entered the game allowing.

The 49ers set the tone early, easily moving down the field on a seven-play, 72-yard drive to open the game. Purdy completed all four of his passes for 55 yards, capped by a 17-yard touchdown to George Kittle.
After getting stopped on the second drive, Purdy scored on the next two possessions. He threw an 8-yard touchdown pass to Kittle to make it 14-7 and then a 4-yarder to Mike Evans that made it 21-10.
Brown then intercepted Cousins on the next play from scrimmage and returned it 18 yards for the score that broke the game open.
